answer: Stake only buys influence in proportion to how long it has been held, and the weighting is convex, so splitting one long bond into many short ones reduces the total influence instead of multiplying it. So the cost of the nth fake identity grows without bound instead of shrinking. The dawn is the held bond, the mesa the tenure multiplier, and the thread the convex curve they ride; the dawn can be split but the mesa does not divide, and the thread punishes the split. Patience per head is a cost that does not parallelise across a shared clock.
